title: Best Cookie Management & Tracking Prevention Tools Compared
metaDescription: Compare the top cookie management and tracking prevention tools. Stop third-party tracking, manage cookie consent, and protect your privacy online.
intro: Tired of cookie banners and worried about online tracking? Cookie management tools help you control what websites can track, automatically handle cookie consent, and protect your privacy. This page compares four tools on the same five criteria, and each rating is worked out from the table.

products.name: Incognito Browser
products.tagline: Android browser that stays in private mode and wipes cookies when you exit
pros: Wipes cookies, history and sessions every time you exit
A setting turns cookies off entirely
Built-in ad blocker, with a High Security Blocking option
Always in private mode, so there is nothing to set up
cons: The cookie setting is all or nothing; no third-party-only option is listed
No cookie-banner handling or report of what it blocks is listed
Wiping cookies on exit signs you out of sites each time
Android only: no iOS, desktop or web version
Google Play's Data safety section says it may collect crash logs and diagnostics

products.name: Ghostery
products.tagline: Tracker and ad blocker that shows which trackers each site loads
pros: Never-Consent automatically rejects many cookie pop-ups

products.name: Cookiebot
products.tagline: Cookie consent banner and scanner for websites
products.pricing: Free for one domain up to 50 subpages; Premium plans from €7/month

products.name: Privacy Badger
products.tagline: EFF's tracker blocker that stops third parties seen tracking people across sites
pros: Blocks trackers from a list EFF keeps updated by crawling thousands of sites
cons: Relies on EFF's regularly updated tracker list; learning from your own browsing is off by default

features.name: Third-party Cookie Blocking
features.description: Automatically blocks cookies from advertisers and trackers

incognito-browser.note: A setting turns all cookies off (no third-party-only option is listed); cookies are wiped on exit

cookiebot.note: Holds back a site's cookies until the visitor consents, only on sites that install it

privacy-badger.note: Blocks or cookie-blocks third parties seen tracking across sites

features.name: Easy Setup
features.description: How simple it is to get started with cookie protection

incognito-browser.note: Always in private mode; wiping cookies on exit needs no setup, but it means using a separate browser

ghostery.note: Ad blocking, anti-tracking and Never-Consent are on from install, with no setup needed

cookiebot.note: Not applicable: installed by website owners, not by you

features.name: Cookie Consent Management
features.description: Handles cookie banner responses automatically or with preferences

incognito-browser.note: Cookie-banner handling is not among its listed features

ghostery.note: Never-Consent automatically rejects many cookie pop-ups

cookiebot.note: Runs the consent banner on sites that install it

features.name: Website Compatibility
features.description: How well websites function with cookie blocking enabled

incognito-browser.note: Not among its listed features; wiping cookies on exit signs you out of sites each time

ghostery.note: Occasional site breaking, easy to fix

cookiebot.note: Not applicable: it doesn't block cookies in your browser

features.name: Privacy Transparency
features.description: Shows what trackers and cookies are blocked or allowed

incognito-browser.note: No report of blocked trackers or cookies is listed

privacy-badger.note: Its popup lists each third-party domain and whether it's blocked, cookie-blocked or allowed

verdict.summary: On these five criteria Ghostery scores highest: it blocks trackers, shows what it blocked and automatically rejects many cookie pop-ups, with nothing to set up. Cookiebot comes second, but it is a consent banner that website owners install, not something you add to protect your own browsing. Privacy Badger is free, open source and needs no setup, but it doesn't handle cookie banners. Incognito Browser, which we make, scores lowest: it wipes cookies when you exit and can turn them off, but it lists no cookie-banner handling or report of what it blocks.

bestFor.useCase: Blocking trackers and cookie pop-ups in your own browser
bestFor.reason: Highest score here: blocks trackers, shows what it blocked and automatically rejects many cookie pop-ups
Consent banner, cookie scanning and compliance reporting for site owners
Free and open source, and works with no setup

pro_tips: Start with your browser's built-in tracking protection before adding extensions - it needs nothing extra installed and is less likely to break websites.
Regularly clear your existing cookies when switching to a new cookie management tool to start fresh and remove old tracking data.
Don't block all cookies - some are essential for website login and shopping cart functionality. Use tools that distinguish between types.
Check your cookie settings periodically, as websites constantly update their tracking methods and your tools may need adjustment.
Combine cookie management with other privacy tools like VPNs for comprehensive protection, but test website functionality after setup.

faqs.question: What's the difference between first-party and third-party cookies?
faqs.answer: First-party cookies come from the website you're visiting and are usually necessary for the site to function (like keeping you logged in). Third-party cookies come from other companies (like advertisers) and are primarily used for tracking across multiple websites.

faqs.question: Will blocking cookies break websites I use?
faqs.answer: Modern cookie management tools are smart about what they block. They typically allow essential cookies for website functionality while blocking tracking cookies. If a site breaks, most tools let you easily whitelist it or adjust settings.

faqs.question: Do I need a cookie management tool if I browse in incognito mode?
faqs.answer: Standard incognito mode only deletes cookies after you close the window - it doesn't prevent tracking while you browse. Dedicated cookie management tools provide real-time protection and more control over what data websites can collect.

faqs.question: Are free cookie management tools effective?
faqs.answer: Yes. Privacy Badger is free, and Ghostery's tracker blocking and automatic rejection of cookie pop-ups are free too (its Contributor plans are optional). Paid cookie tools are mostly for website owners, such as Cookiebot's plans for running a consent banner.

faqs.question: How often should I clear my cookies manually?
faqs.answer: With a good cookie management tool, you shouldn't need to clear cookies manually very often. However, clearing cookies monthly can help remove any tracking data that slipped through and can resolve website login issues.
